sources.citation: De Marco, Barbara & Jerry R. Craddock (transcr./rev.). 2013 [preface updated 2015]. Relacion de Hernan Gallegos sobre la expedicion del padre fray Agustin Rodriguez y el capitan Francisco Sanchez Chamuscado a Nuevo Mexico, 1581-1582. Archivo General de Indias, Sevilla, Patronato 22, ramo 4, fols. 71r-100v (with appendices). Cibola Project, Research Center for Romance Studies, University of California, Berkeley. eScholarship item 4sv5h1gz.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonology content. The relation embeds five native items in running Spanish narrative, written without any accent marks: fol. 30r/74r 'los quales respondieron que se llamaba "amotomaulo". Llaman al agua "abad", al mayz "tooy" y a los frisoles "ayaguate"'; fol. 31v/75v 'llaman aquel cobre "parla"'; fol. 32v/76v 'alcan las manos hazia el sol y dizen en su lengua en mudanca de baile "ayoa canima" y lo hazen con mucho conpas y horden.. por el buen consonante y tono que le dan' ('tono' here = the tune of the dance song, not linguistic tone). Wordlist-level data only; no statement about accent,…

sources.citation: Ahern, Maureen. 2001. La Relacion y concudio de Hernan Gallegos: glosa, guia y memoria de Nuevo Mexico 1581-1582. Lexis (PUCP, Lima) 25(1-2): 381-406. doi:10.18800/lexis.20010102.019
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonology content; nothing on the Amotomanco forms. Read pp. 389-391 and searched the full text for amotomanco/otomoaco/abad/teoy/ayaguate/canima/acento (only bibliography hit for Troike). File not kept (not about this languoid's language).

sources.citation: Craddock, Jerry R. 1996. Philological Notes on the Hammond and Rey Translation of the [Relacion de la] Entrada que hizo en el Nuevo Mexico Francisco Sanchez Chamuscado en junio de [15]81 by Hernan Gallegos, Notary of the Expedition. Romance Philology 49: 351-363. Electronic reprint with supplements (facsimiles, lexical and grammatical notes, 14-note case file), Cibola Project, UC Berkeley, 2008 (rev. 2023). eScholarship item 8sj8g6nj, 58 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or tone; the work is about transcription/translation errors in Hammond & Rey. Relevant datum: the MS reading of the passage is given as 'Los quales rrespondieron que se llamaba amotomau-|co. Llaman al agua abad al mayz to oy y a los frisoles ayaguate' -- i.e. the language name 'Amotomanco' of the secondary literature rests on H&R's reading of amotomauco, and 'teoy' on a reading of 'to oy'/'tooy'. The article pages (351-363) are facsimile images without a text layer in the PDF; only the supplements' text was machine-readable and read; the article body was not scanned because…
